correctness.rationale: Exact mixed factorial moments on component types yield independent Poisson limits with rational means. All Gaifman degrees are at most two; closed finite-radius types reduce to bounded-size components while each nonclosed type saturates using arbitrarily many distinct odd-length paths. Effective Hanf locality reduces each fixed FO sentence to finite Poisson-count tests, yielding rational polynomials in a common exponential. Independent odd-path-existence indicators give arbitrarily fine Boolean atom partitions and hence a dense logical limit spectrum. Finite enumeration tests only the exact moments, not the infinite statements.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the algebraic form and topological density of every fixed first-order limiting probability for a natural ensemble of two random involutions. This identifies substantially richer logical behavior than a zero–one law and is motivated by the standard first-order limit-law problem; it is not merely the classical enumerative EGF or a single-component computation.
